speaker: Doctor
text:
Can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes of unresponsiveness, and do you notice any specific triggers or patterns?  

REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram)  
REQUEST IMAGES: If you have any prior imaging or video recordings of the episodes, please provide them.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: EEG Findings: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations. Social history: Enrolled in second grade. Lives with parents and one sibling. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, headache, visual or auditory disturbances, weakness, or other systemic symptoms. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand your concern, but skipping the diagnostic process could lead to an incorrect conclusion; I need to determine if these episodes involve loss of consciousness or simply staring. Has anyone observed if you lose awareness of your surroundings during these events, or do you just appear confused?

REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram)
REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide any video recordings of an episode if possible.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: EEG Findings: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Temporal Lobe Epilepsy. The presence of interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the right temporal lobe, combined with your history of unresponsiveness and facial grimacing, is highly diagnostic of focal seizures originating in this region.
